rationale: The mechanism-as-execution argument is clean: the visitor's clock and locale literally enact On Kawara's studio rules, and the midnight repaint enacts his destruction rule. The Esperanto fallback for non-Roman scripts is a genuinely literate double-coding touch. However, this work is materially identical to the already-catalogued 'Today (2026)' entry — same source (On Kawara), same mechanism (per-visit Intl locale render with midnight repaint, zero persistence), same argument. G6 fails on duplication. Novelty is also low because the work has already been claimed in the catalogue.
reservations: G6 failure: the candidate is a duplicate of the existing 'Today (2026)' catalogue entry. The mechanism, source, and argument are essentially the same. Even setting duplication aside, the work sits comfortably inside territory already mapped by la-trahison-des-images.be (mechanism-as-message) and The webpage going on and off (live, self-erasing render loop), so its novelty of ontology is modest.
revision_suggestion: To pass G6, either (a) pick a materially different source — e.g. a Kawara-adjacent but distinct gesture like the I Am Still Alive telegrams, or a different conceptual-art destruction/per-day rule (Hanne Darboven's calculations, Felix Gonzalez-Torres' candy piles that must be eaten) — or (b) keep Kawara but change the mechanism substantially: e.g. a multi-timezone 'today' grid that paints every timezone's current date simultaneously, or a bot that tweets one destroyed painting per day with no image retained. The current build is too close to the existing entry to be a new work.
